statement: The function returns a result r and r equals the number of pairs (i, j) of indices with 0 <= i <= j < len(nums) such that nums[i] = nums[j] and, for every k with i <= k <= j, nums[k] <= nums[i].
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 10^9.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, len(nums) <= r <= len(nums) * (len(nums) + 1) / 2.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 10^9.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, if nums[i] != nums[j] for all i, j with 0 <= i < j < len(nums), then r = len(nums).
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 10^9.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, if the array nums is non-decreasing (nums[i] <= nums[i+1] for all 0 <= i < len(nums)-1) or non-increasing (nums[i] >= nums[i+1] for all 0 <= i < len(nums)-1), then r equals the number of pairs (i, j) with 0 <= i <= j < len(nums) and nums[i] = nums[j].
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 10^9.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, let m = len(nums) and define the reversed array b by b[i] = nums[m-1-i] for 0 <= i < m. Then r equals the number of pairs (i, j) with 0 <= i <= j < m such that b[i] = b[j] and b[k] <= b[i] for every k with i <= k <= j.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 10^9.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, if f is any strictly increasing function from the set of values occurring in nums to the 64-bit integers (i.e., f(x) < f(y) whenever x < y for x, y in that set), and b is defined by b[i] = f(nums[i]) for 0 <= i < len(nums), then r equals the number of pairs (i, j) with 0 <= i <= j < len(nums) such that b[i] = b[j] and b[k] <= b[i] for every k with i <= k <= j.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 10^9.

statement: For every input nums satisfying the preconditions, the function returns a result r (it does not fail due to arithmetic overflow, out-of-bounds indexing, or panic).
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 10^9.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r > len(nums) if and only if there exist indices i and j with 0 <= i < j < len(nums), nums[i] = nums[j], and nums[k] <= nums[i] for every k with i <= k <= j.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 10^9.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for each j with 0 <= j < len(nums), let c(j) be the number of indices i with 0 <= i <= j such that nums[i] = nums[j] and nums[k] <= nums[i] for every k with i <= k <= j. Then r = sum_{j=0}^{len(nums)-1} c(j).
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 10^9.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, let E be the number of pairs (i, j) with 0 <= i <= j < len(nums) and nums[i] = nums[j]. Then r <= E.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 10^9.
